title: WPMS/434/2018 of SHEKHAR RASTOGI Vs STATE OF UTTARAKHAND THROUGH SECRETARY REVENUE DEPARTMENT

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND
AT NAINITAL
ON THE 28TH DAY OF MAY, 2021
BEFORE:
HON'BLE SHRI JUSTICE MANOJ KUMAR TIWARI
Writ Petition (M/S) No. 434 of 2018
BETWEEN:
Shekhar Rastogi ......Petitioner
(By Mr. B.S. Koranga, Advocate, holding brief of Mr. M.K. Ray, Advocate)
AND:
State of Uttarakhand & others .....Respondents
(By Mr. J.S. Bisht, Standing Counsel for the State of
Uttarakhand/respondents)
JUDGMENT
Heard learned counsel for the parties through video
conferencing.
2. By means of this writ petition, petitioner has sought
following relief:
"(A) issue a writ order or direction in the nature of
mandamus directing the respondent no. 3 to issue
a caste certificate to the petitioner forthwith."
3. According to the petitioner, he belongs to 'Sunar
Community', which is identified as Other Backward Class;
but, O.B.C. Caste Certificate is being denied to him.
4. A counter affidavit has been filed by Tehsildar,
Kichha, District Udham Singh Nagar. In para no. 4 of the
said counter affidavit, it has been stated that Annexure
No.-4 to the writ petition is an application made by the
petitioner for issuance of Permanent Resident Certificate,
and when application is for Permanent Resident
Certificate, then caste certificate cannot be issued to him
pursuant to such application. In para no. 5 of the counter
affidavit, it has been further stated that for issuance of

2
Permanent Resident Certificate, certain documents are
required to be submitted, as stipulated in Government
Order dated 20.11.2001, however, petitioner has not
furnished those documents, in support of his claim for
Permanent Resident Certificate.
5. From perusal of the record, it is apparent that there
is no application filed by the petitioner for issuance of
Caste Certificate and there is only one application
enclosed as Annexure-4, which is for issuance of
Permanent/Original Resident Certificate.
6. In such view of the matter, the relief, as claimed in
the writ petition, cannot be granted.
7. Accordingly, writ petition is dismissed.
8. However, it is made clear that if petitioner makes
application for issuance of Permanent Resident Certificate
and O.B.C. Certificate, then Competent Authority shall
examine petitioner's claim and take appropriate decision
thereupon, in accordance with law, as early as possible,
preferably within six months from the date of receipt of
application along with certified copy of this order.
 (MANOJ KUMAR TIWARI, J.) Navin
